subject: dplyr table-joining verbs: copy argument has no effect for sql tbls?

messages.author: 693e8dae13e7c1ad
messages.subject: dplyr table-joining verbs: copy argument has no effect for sql tbls?
parts:
Hello all,

I was looking through the code for left_join, and noticed something strange. left_join.tbl_sql calls auto_copy, passing it the copy argument. auto_copy.tbl_sql in turn calls copy_to, but _doesn't_ pass the copy argument. Does this mean that, when joining with a database table x, the table y will always be copied, even if it's located in the same database?

As a corollary, does this mean that y is always turned into a data frame in the global environment (as per the code in auto_copy)? Surely this can't be right; y could potentially be a gigantic table that won't fit into memory.

This is the source code I'm referring to:

> dplyr:::left_join.tbl_sql
function (x, y, by = NULL, copy = FALSE, auto_index = FALSE, 
    ...) 
{
    by <- common_by(by, x, y)
    y <- auto_copy(x, y, copy, indexes = if (auto_index) 
        list(by$y))
    sql <- sql_join(x$src$con, x, y, type = "left", by = by)
    update(tbl(x$src, sql), group_by = groups(x))
}


> dplyr:::auto_copy.tbl_sql
function (x, y, copy = FALSE, ...) 
{
    copy_to(x$src, as.data.frame(y), random_table_name(), ...)
}


What am I missing here?
